name: Southern Sea-Gull
notes:
The big dark-backed gull of the southern coasts, on every rock where a boat comes in. It follows the trawlers out and the fish-gutters home, and a harbour with no gulls over it is a harbour where nobody is landing anything. Not the Sky-Gull of the floating islands, which is a smaller white bird that has never seen a fishing boat.

Slate on the back and wings, white everywhere else, and a heavy yellow bill that will open a shellfish the gull has dropped on a rock twice. The fishers say a gull standing still on a rock means the weather will hold, and a gull walking means it will not.
journal_prompt: A big gull on the landing rock, slate-backed, yellow-billed, standing on one spot with the patience of something that knows the boats come back.
appearance: A large gull, white on the head, neck and underparts, with a dark slate-grey back and wings, black wingtips with small white spots, a heavy hooked yellow bill, pale yellow eyes and pinkish-orange legs.
